jobs.title: Gully meets him
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, hair longer, brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands always in its pockets; GULLY — aged 20, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Gully and the dog. Instant. Wood watches an alliance form. Panel 1: a small dog lunging joyfully toward a boy in a backwards cap on a wooden dock, dragging a young man in a chore coat by the leash, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: GULLY, WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: a boy in a backwards cap kneeling on a dock laughing while a scruffy dog climbs all over him (in this panel: GULLY, BARNABY (the dog)). Gully says "Who's this.". Wood says "Barnaby. He was behind the Lanes.". Gully says "He smells like the Lanes.". Panel 3: close-up of a boy holding out a maple bar to a transfixed small dog, a hand reaching to stop him too late (in this panel: GULLY, BARNABY (the dog)). Wood says "Don't—". Gully says "Half.". Panel 4: a boy in a backwards cap and a small dog sitting side by side on the edge of a dock over the water, a young man behind them drawing, black and white (in this panel: GULLY, BARNABY (the dog), WOOD). Wood says, in a small balloon, "Traitor.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby.
